entities.summary:
The assassination of Andrei Karlov on 2016-12-19 had far-reaching consequences for global diplomacy and security.

The attack occurred at the opening of an art exhibition in Ankara, Turkey, when the Russian ambassador was deliberately targeted and killed by a lone gunman. This event was a significant turning point in the tumultuous relationship between Russia and Turkey, with long-lasting impacts on regional politics.

The assassination led to a marked escalation of tensions between the two nations, with repercussions felt across the Middle East and beyond. It also raised questions about the safety of diplomats and the vulnerability of high-profile targets in a rapidly changing global landscape.

In the aftermath of the assassination, Turkish-Russian relations continued to deteriorate, with both sides engaging in a war of words and diplomatic maneuvers. The event served as a stark reminder of the fragility of international relations and the ease with which a single act of violence can have far-reaching and devastating consequences.

As Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov noted in a statement after the assassination, "This is a tragic event, and we condemn it in the strongest possible terms."
